texts.preamble: Surajmal Son Of Jagdish Narayan vs Chandra Prakash S/O Jagdish Narayan on 26 April, 2024 Author: Narendra Singh Dhaddha
texts.facts: This order disposes of S.B. Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.990/2023 filed by the appellant-applicant-Surajmal (for short 'the applicant') challenging the order dated 07.01.2023 passed by the trial court in application No.13/2020 (37/19), whereby the trial court partly dismissed the temporary injunction application filed by the applicant. It also disposes of S.B. Cross Objection (Civil) No. 26/2023 filed by respondent No.1-non-applicant (for [2024:RJ-JP:19507] (4 of 7) [CMA-990/2023] short 'non-applicant No.1') against the said order passed by the trial court, whereby the trial court partly allowed the temporary injunction application filed by the applicant and restrained the non-applicant Nos.1 to 3 and 6 to 11 to dispose of, transfer and/or to cause interference/hurdle in using and occupying the suit property as mentioned in para 5 of temporary injunction application by the applicant qua his share and rights therein.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the order dated 07.01.2023 passed by the trial court is not based on sound principle of law because the trial court had not considered all the relevant documents, pleadings of the parties and restrained the non-applicant Nos.1 to 3 and 6 to 11 to dispose of, transfer and/or to cause interfere/hindrance in using and occupying the suit property as mentioned in para 5 of the application by the applicant qua his share and right therein. Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that the trial court had wrongly declined the prayer of the temporary injunction regarding property mentioned in para No.6 and 7 of the temporary injunction application. Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that the trial court wrongly came to the conclusion that applicant did not rebut the averment of non-applicant No.1 that he had received the compensation against the acquisition of Chandralok Hotel. Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that mere non-filing of rejoinder does not tantamount to admission of applicant. Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that the applicant in its plaint as well as in temporary injunction application clearly stated that properties mentioned in para No.5, 6 and 7 of the application are Joint Hindu Property. Properties mentioned in para 6 and 7 of the temporary [2024:RJ-JP:19507] (5 of 7) [CMA-990/2023] injunction application were purchased in the name of non- applicant No.1 but these were purchased from Joint Hindu Family income as well as income of Surajmal Son Of Jagdish Narayan vs Chandra Prakash S/O Jagdish Narayan on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128971352/ 3 the Chandralok Hotel. Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that applicant had submitted the documents in this regard. Criminal case was filed against the applicant under Section 7 (i)/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Income Tax doucments were filed in which applicant was shown as proprietor of Chandralok Hotel. Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that non-applicant No.1 had failed to adduce the documentary evidence that he had purchased the properties mentioned in para 6 and 7 of temporary injunction application, out of his personal income. These properties were Joint Hindu properties or not would be decided after taking evidence of the parties. So, the trial court had to direct to maintain the status quo regarding the disputed properties mentioned in para 6 and 7 of the temporary injunction application as well. Learned counsel for the non-applicant No.1 has also filed the cross-objection against the order dated 07.01.2023 and submits that the trial court rightly came to the conclusion that these properties were in the name of non-applicant No.1. Non-applicant No.1 also got the compensation against the acquisition and after conversion of the said land, he sold part of land to Satya Narayan [2024:RJ-JP:19507] (6 of 7) [CMA-990/2023] Gupta and Deep Kanwar. At that time, applicant and other non- applicants had not objected the said sale. Learned counsel for the non-applicant No.1 also submits that if the trial court had exercised its discretion while adjudicating the temporary injunction application then scope of the appellate court is very limited. So, present appeal being devoid of merit, is liable to be dismissed and also submitted that the order of the trial court granting temporary injunction application regarding property mentioned in para 5 of temporary injunction application is also required to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Learned counsel for the non-applicant No.1 has placed reliance upon the following judgments : (1) Parshuram & Anr. Vs. Vishwanath & Ors. reported in 2019 (Suppl.) Civil Court Cases 083 (Rajasthan); (2) Mohd. Mehtab Khan & Ors. Vs. Khushnuma Ibrahim Khan & Ors. reported in 2013 (9) SCC 221 and (3) Tamil Nadu Housing Board Vs. Master Crafts, Partnership Firm reported in 2011 (3) CTC 650.
